concern_results.conclusion: Traced ownership checks, version comparison, dry-run/update/uninstall flows, and recovery through antigravity-adapter.ts plus the unified.ts dispatch and probe mapping; state transitions produce the documented statuses with no wrong-state path found.

Every mutation of the plugin tree requires a byte-for-byte receipt match first; unowned, drifted, unlisted, and forged-journal states are refused without host changes, backups and journals stay under the verified ~/.gemini components, and symlink/traversal guards cover the managed root.

Journal is written before host mutation, reconcile recovers or refuses without trusting journal contents, and the fail-after-install compensation (including reinstall from the verified backup for updates) restores prior state or returns partial with journal and backup retained as evidence.

The new suite covers round-trip, unowned/drift refusals, pre- and post-mutation install failure rollback, update/downgrade/failed-update backup restore, journal recovery, forged-journal rejection, unmanaged roots, lock contention, disabled and malformed host state, and missing CLI; each risky behavior has an assertion that fails if it regresses.

The change is additive first-class Antigravity support matching the requester's scope with no push/PR surface; existing claude/codex/opencode dispatch is untouched and no unrequested flags, gates, or refactors were added.

README and source-register claims (receipt byte-match refusal, verified backup rollback, hook binding parity, busy shared lock) are carried by code and tests in the candidate; no absolutes or exhaustiveness claims exceed what the packet's evidence shows.

The diff honors the quoted contracts: no version field in the .antigravity-plugin manifest, the npm test enforces hooks/hooks.json parity with agy-bridge.py bindings as the root contract requires, host registration mutates only via the public agy CLI, runtime dependencies stay at zero, and tests use isolated fake-host fixtures that prove rollback explicitly.

challenge_focus: Delta review after the adversarial challenge. The npm Antigravity adapter was narrowed (no snapshots: install from the bundled plugin, receipt of file hashes, temporary verified backup for update rollback, journal records only that an operation was in flight, shared lock with scripts/install-antigravity.sh). The checkout installer now records a full file-hash inventory and refreshes only on an exact match. The bridge stopped lexical path collapsing, uses workspacePaths only when it is a single absolute directory, allows only plainly harmless commands when the merge guard cannot run, checks every patch target before returning ask, and bounds its run-lock wait inside the event deadline. Check these fixes for regressions and remaining data-loss or bypass paths. Requester asked: first-class Antigravity host support, no push or PR.
